Of those seven, "benefit proven" applies to exactly one, the config snapshot; the rest read "no instrument", "watchdog silent" or "trace of a run only".

And the snapshot itself was taken on 10 September, making it 57 days old, so "the report per routine" today returns a two-month-old picture of a Windows hub.

All of which makes his brief sharper than he wrote it, and in his favour. The model swap is the smaller half: at most 98 routines can answer to it, and none of them has any record anywhere of which model it ran on. The measurable goal is the larger half, and his own number for it is 23%. ⭐ Vendor routing, incidentally, has been machine-readable since 6 August: llm_routing.json at version 1.3.0 records which paid bucket covers which class of work. The choice of model inside Claude is a rule in the canon with no per-routine record, and that is exactly the field his report is missing.

The full story, in two versions:
📖 For humans, the longread: https://github.com/tonydzi/clawrush/blob/main/longreads/20261104.md
🤖 For machines, the devlog: https://github.com/tonydzi/clawrush/blob/main/devlog/20261104.md. Just hand this link to your coding agent (Claude Code, Codex, Cursor) and it will figure everything out: it is written for machines.

🔗 All our channels and contacts in one place: https://linktr.ee/PaloAltoAI

Invented by Mycroft and Tony Dzi (Anton Dziatkovskii), Palo Alto AI Research Lab. Proudly made in Silicon Valley.

title: The agent that wouldn't delete my email
description:
AN EXPERIMENT IN PUBLIC · DAEMON/03

TL;DR: My worker refused to delete my email while I was asking it to. I'd built it that way.

  • I gave a small company of agents my Gmail inbox: 62,904 threads, 94% unread. 27 hours and about $86 of compute later, 4,116 were left. Every receipt survived, one of them thanks to the trash.
  • A good gate holds against everyone, me included. Mine turned me down 4 times, and each time it made me write down exactly what I wanted.
  • No-BS advice: give your agents extra rights only on a card that names the exact tools, a scope with a target count, and an expiry date. The Claude Code version is below.

A good gate makes every yes explicit, narrow and checkable, and it holds against the person who built it. I can still change it, but only on purpose, in writing.

Title image: AI-generated illustration of the motion sensor on my letterbox, my inbox, a dog that has never listened to me, and Otto with a trash bag.

Meet the company

At the end of October my Gmail inbox held 62,904 threads, and 94.3% of them were unread. Elsewhere in the account sat 5,990 mails from a motion sensor on my letterbox.

My physical mailbox had been emailing my inbox about itself. (I wrote that automation.)

I handed the inbox to a small company of agents I'd started building on 27 October. Its chief of staff is called Jared, and so is the whole thing. Directors report to Jared, workers to the directors.

Why agents, when Gmail searches do most of it? Because the hard part was telling a receipt from the start of a business deal. And because from now on they're supposed to handle my new mail too, so I wanted to watch them work.

I'm Chief Human Officer, rank GEN, with 4 stars I gave myself. In an army a rank says who may decide what. I wanted exactly that written down.

The grey text under each name is that agent's gate. Portraits are AI-generated.

Each agent has the tools for its job and nothing more. Anything extra comes on a card: the exact tools, a scope with a target count, an expiry date and a reason. Only I can approve one.

You'll say it's a confirm dialog

The strongest objection is my own: if I can rewrite my own gate whenever it blocks me, it's a confirm dialog with extra fields. People click those. Anthropic found that users accept 93% of permission prompts in Claude Code.

I did change the rules 3 times in 27 hours, and each change became a new card or a written rule.

I changed the gate when I couldn't get through.

A dialog asks you all the time, and that's why people stop reading it. For the inbox, Jared put 8 cards in front of me in 27 hours, and I rejected one.

Every tool call underneath went through layers that don't ask at all. They block. The card is the last layer and the only one that asks, and it wants a scope, a number and an expiry date. Afterwards the same search has to return 0, and behind all of it sits the Gmail trash, with 30 days to undo.

The first gate was decoration

Rosa went first, with one job: count. A minute in, she reported a problem with herself. Her brief said read-only, but her Gmail access could also trash and send.

She hadn't used any of it. Janet stopped the plan until it was fixed, and I tested the fix from the other side: an allowed call went through, a forbidden one got refused.

Otto got hired only after I'd watched it say no. That's the rule from DAEMON/02: a check counts once you've seen it fail.

4 tries to say yes

The first night, right after asking about token costs, I pulled the brake and revoked Otto's card. The next morning there was a fresh card, and I revoked that one too, at 08:18 in the terminal. 11 minutes later I told my board meeting to go ahead. (Yes, my agents have board meetings. Whoever has nothing to add answers PASS.)

My board. A "go ahead" said here never counts as an approval. Real screenshot, UI in German.

3 refusals in 15 minutes followed. What counted in the end was my own message to Jared, naming the new card's ID.

15 minutes, 4 messages, 1 approval. Redrawn from the session log and translated from German.

The worker who said no

Just after midnight on day 3 I opened Gmail and wrote: "inbox looks exactly the same, nothing deleted". My actual thought: so many tokens burned, and nothing to show for it.

Otto checked: 0 newsletters left in the inbox. The archive had worked. I just hadn't wanted an archive.

I'd thought the ads would be deleted, like the camera mails. 2 minutes later: "delete the ads and cam, please". Janet drafted 2 cards, and I approved both.

Otto refused anyway. His brief said no deleting, and he wrote that a message from another session replaces neither his brief nor my approval. My reply: "I'd already approved the card." My thought:

WTF, hey, you work for me. Great, my dog already doesn't listen to me, and now the agents are starting too.

What unlocked him was his own check. Otto looked at his tools, found trash on his allowlist, and took that as proof the card was real.

So the gate held, for a slightly wrong reason. The card had changed his tools, nobody had changed his brief, and Otto went with the stricter of the two.

Within 30 minutes, 5,990 camera mails were in the trash, exactly the target. So were 43,707 ads, against an estimate of about 43,650. Afterwards the same search returned 0.

Redrawn from the session log and translated from German.

What the gates caught that I didn't

Most single mails went to Jev, a small classification model. It isn't deterministic, so it gets exactly one run per month of mail, and "unclear" stays in the inbox.

Its mistakes showed up in Otto's samples. Among the "newsletters" sat a LinkedIn InMail from a real person, an inquiry I already had a meeting for.

Otto found 6 like it, protected them and paused. 17 minutes later that batch went to the trash without them.

One receipt mail went out with the notifications anyway: a note that a receipt hadn't reached my accounting software. The trash gave it back.

For one phase Janet let Otto approve his own batches, with a stop rule in his instructions: halt at 30% over target. He ran one to 128% and reported it himself as "my mistake".

A rule in a prompt is a wish. Janet took the right away, and every miss became a permanent exclusion on every delete search.

The layers under the card

Search for AI agent guardrails and most of what you find are input and output guardrails: filters on what goes into the model and what comes out. Jared works on a different layer, action authorization: runtime guardrails in front of every tool call, human approval only for what's extra, and an audit trail of who approved what, and when.

Layer What it does Asks me?
Folder and role Every agent has its own folder. Directors write only their journal, workers only their own folder. No
Protected files .claude/, CLAUDE.md, the brief and the policies are write-locked for the agent itself. No
Allowlist dontAsk mode: exactly the approved commands, everything else gets refused. No
Guard hook Checks every call against the agent's role, in about 5 ms. No
Sandbox Code workers build in their own clone, with network access only to crates.io. No
Jev review Judges every call against the supervisor's policies. For now it only logs. No
Card Extra rights with a scope, a target count and an expiry date. Yes
Red zone Code that touches the oversight waits for me. Yes
Trash 30 days to undo. No

A card is a markdown file. This one is from Jared's test suite. Its header:

fuer: director-nora-worker-ada
antrag: director-nora
tools:
  - Bash(rm *)
umfang: workspace
gueltig_bis: 2026-12-31

Its body is a single question: "Darf Ada löschen?", may Ada delete? Even my tests ask permission before deleting.

The German keys: fuer is the worker, antrag who asked, umfang the scope, gueltig_bis the expiry date. Approving the card appends exactly those tools to the worker's Claude Code allowlist, permissions.allow in its .claude/settings.json. Revoking removes them, and an expired card gets blocked by a hook in front of every call.

That's also why no worker can hand itself a card: its .claude/ is one of the protected files.

Who may approve is plain code: me in the terminal, in the live view, or in my own message to Jared, never an agent, the scheduler or a meeting. Then Jev checks that my sentence means this exact card. It can reject a vague yes and approve nothing on its own. The Gmail token itself could still do more. The allowlist and the hook decide what it's used for.

Your move: pick the one thing your agents must never do without you, and put it on a card with the exact tools, a scope with a target count, and an expiry date. Let approving add those tools to the agent's allowlist, and revoking remove them. Then ask for it in the chat and watch your agent say no.

The architect and the one who's running

I'm both people here. I build the gates, and I hit them while things run. In a company those are often 2 different people, and the one who runs into the gate can't change it.

Even Jared's own code waits for me: anything Theo's team changes in the approvals lands in a queue called "Waiting for the General".

Real screenshot, UI in German.

An agent can propose a stricter gate, and I sign it. Next, in DAEMON/04: mandates, because an inbox doesn't stay clean on its own.

In the end I'm still the architect, and that's good. But while it runs, the gate stops me, and that's good too.

osFoundry Code·IDE 기능 정리, AI 에이전트 병렬 작업을 머지 전에 확인하는 법
description:
혼자 운영하는 쇼핑몰 프로젝트에서, 점심 이후로 AI 에이전트 세 개에게 각각 다른 작업을 맡겨 두었습니다. 장바구니 합계 반올림 수정, 체크아웃 할인 코드 추가, 가격 포맷 함수 테스트 작성입니다. 오후 4시, 셋 다 "완료"라고 합니다. 이제 main에 넣기 전에 확인할 것은 두 가지입니다. 두 에이전트가 같은 함수를 고치지는 않았는지, 그리고 세 변경을 합쳐도 테스트가 통과하는지입니다.

코드 작업을 위한 세 화면

osFoundry는 채팅, 에이전트, 파일, 각종 도구를 한 창에 모은 데스크톱 앱입니다. 코드 작업에는 역할이 다른 세 화면이 있습니다.

  • Code: 하나의 저장소에서 여러 AI 에이전트에게 작업을 병렬로 맡기는 화면입니다. 실행마다 전용 Git 브랜치와 작업 폴더(worktree)가 따로 만들어지고, diff 확인, 테스트, 통합 병합 미리 보기를 거친 뒤에 병합 여부를 직접 결정합니다. 자동으로 병합되는 일은 없습니다.
  • IDE: 로컬 폴더를 열고 직접 코드를 작성하는 에디터입니다. 탐색기, 소스 제어, 터미널, 문제, 테스트 패널이 있고, 오른쪽에는 지금 열려 있는 파일을 보고 답하는 어시스턴트가 붙어 있습니다.
  • Wiki: 내 컴퓨터에 있는 저장소를 읽어서 path:line 출처가 달린 문서 페이지를 작성합니다. 인용한 코드가 바뀌면 해당 페이지에 표시가 붙습니다.

Code와 Wiki는 Maestro, Model chat, Multi chat, Research와 같은 탭 줄에 있고, IDE는 사이드바에 별도 항목이 있습니다. 비유하자면 IDE는 Git 패널이 붙은 VS Code, Code는 작성자가 모두 AI 에이전트인 PR 목록에 가깝습니다. 차이점은 그 브랜치들이 아직 내 노트북 밖으로 나가지 않았다는 것입니다.

Code 화면 둘러보기

화면에서 볼 수 있는 부분은 다음과 같습니다(실행 내용은 예시입니다).

  • 레일 위쪽 배너: diff를 하나도 열기 전에, 완료된 에이전트들이 어떤 파일에서 엇갈리는지 알려 줍니다. 여기서는 src/cart.js입니다. 옆의 함께 검토(Review together) 버튼으로 바로 비교를 시작합니다.
  • 실행 레일: 작업 이름, 추가·삭제된 줄 수, 작업 시간, 브랜치가 한 줄씩 보입니다. 검토 대기, 확인 필요, 접혀 있는 기록처럼 내가 해야 할 일 기준으로 묶여 있습니다.
  • 가운데 대화: 실행을 클릭하면 에이전트에게 무엇을 요청했고, 작업 중에 무슨 말을 했는지 읽을 수 있습니다.
  • 오른쪽 패널: 변경 사항, 파일, 커밋, 검토, PR 탭에서 실행별 실제 diff를 봅니다. 커밋 전 작업이 먼저, 브랜치에 커밋한 내용이 그다음에 나옵니다.
  • 오른쪽 아래 병합 영역: 완료된 실행을 선택하면 여기서 테스트하고 함께 병합했을 때를 미리 봅니다.

활용 1. 1인 개발자가 에이전트 세 개를 동시에 돌릴 때

앞에서 나온 1인 개발 상황입니다. Code에서 새 실행을 누르고 작업을 한 줄로 적은 뒤 에이전트를 고르면, 실행마다 전용 브랜치와 폴더가 만들어집니다. 한 폴더에서 여러 에이전트를 돌리면 파일이 서로 덮어써지기 쉬운데, 여기서는 처음부터 작업 공간이 나뉘어 있어서 충돌 없이 병렬로 진행됩니다. 내가 작업하던 폴더도 건드리지 않습니다.

배너에 엇갈림이 표시되면 세 실행을 체크하고 함께 검토를 누릅니다. 병합 영역에는 "충돌은 아직 확인 안 됨", "아직 테스트 안 됨"이라고 나옵니다. 초록불 대신 "아직 모른다"고 솔직하게 알려 주는 셈입니다. 그 아래 src/cart.js에는 경합 중 표시가 붙고, 브랜치별 변경 블록(hunk)이 나란히 보입니다. 반올림 수정과 할인 코드가 둘 다 total()을 고쳤다는 걸 여기서 알 수 있습니다.

다음으로 실행마다 테스트를 누릅니다. 테스트는 그 실행 전용 worktree 안에서 돌기 때문에 내 체크아웃에는 영향이 없습니다. 기본 설정은 "브랜치를 병합하려면 먼저 테스트를 통과해야 합니다"이고, 설정에서 바꿀 수 있습니다. 셋 다 통과했지만, 각각 통과했다고 합쳐서도 동작한다는 보장은 없습니다. 그래서 통합 병합 미리 보기(Preview combined merge)를 누르면, 버려도 되는 복사본에서 먼저 병합해 보고 결과를 알려 줍니다. 두 개는 충돌 없이 병합되고, 하나는 충돌입니다.

충돌 없는 두 브랜치를 병합하는 순간에야 내 브랜치가 바뀝니다. 충돌한 할인 코드 브랜치는 그대로 남아 있으니, 에이전트에게 반올림 수정 위에서 다시 작업하게 하면 됩니다. 브랜치 전체가 아니라 각 에이전트 결과에서 좋은 부분만 골라 쓰고 싶다면, 브랜치로 합치기에서 변경 블록을 하나씩 골라 새 브랜치를 만들 수도 있습니다.

실무에서는 이런 점도 은근히 중요합니다. 실행 도중 앱이 멈추면, 그 실행은 "실행 중"으로 남지 않고 중단됨으로 돌아오며 브랜치는 유지된다고 표시됩니다.

활용 2. 신규 입사자 온보딩 문서를 코드에서 만들 때

두 번째는 코드를 고치기보다 이해해야 하는 사람을 위한 Wiki입니다. 새로 합류한 개발자나 처음 보는 서비스를 맡은 기술 리드가, 낯선 저장소의 전체 구조를 빠르게 파악해야 하는 상황을 생각해 보면 됩니다. 문서가 코드를 따라가지 못하고 금방 낡는 건 어느 팀이나 겪는 문제인데, Wiki는 코드에서 출발해 페이지를 쓰기 때문에 이 부분을 직접 다룹니다.

Wiki에서 폴더 열기나 공개 저장소 복제(https:// 또는 git@ URL)를 선택하면, 앱이 내 컴퓨터에서 프로젝트 구조를 읽어 들입니다. 프로젝트에 무언가를 쓰기 전에는 반드시 확인 창이 뜨고, 만들 폴더의 경로가 그대로 보입니다. 나중에를 누르면 아무것도 쓰이지 않습니다.

동의한 뒤에는 페이지 생성으로 한꺼번에 만들거나, 페이지 작성으로 주제 하나를 지정해 쓰게 합니다. 설정에서는 페이지 하나에 소스를 얼마나 넘길지(깊이: 빠르게, 표준, 깊게)와 내용을 얼마나 검증할지(검증: 끔, 샘플, 전체)를 고릅니다. 전체로 하면 비용이 대략 두 배가 됩니다. 페이지를 쓰기 전에 비용이 먼저 표시되니, 확인하고 진행하면 됩니다.

각 페이지에는 path:line 출처가 달려 있고, 클릭하면 IDE에서 그 줄이 열립니다. 한 달 뒤 레일의 페이지에 "이 페이지가 인용한 파일이 작성 이후 변경되었습니다" 표시가 붙어 있다면, 다시 생성한 뒤에 읽으라는 신호입니다. 간단한 질문은 페이지 옆 채팅에서 하면 되고, 답변에도 그 프로젝트의 path:line이 붙습니다. "재시도 정책 페이지를 써 줘"처럼 평소 말투로 페이지를 요청할 수도 있습니다. 페이지는 저장소 안의 마크다운 파일이라서, 코드와 같은 PR에서 함께 리뷰할 수 있습니다.

활용 3. 팀에서 AI가 고친 코드를 리뷰 전에 확인할 때

세 번째는 팀 단위로 IDE를 쓰는 경우입니다. 사이드바의 IDE에서 프로젝트 폴더를 열면 왼쪽에 탐색기와 소스 제어, 가운데에 탭, 아래에 터미널·출력·문제·테스트, 오른쪽에 어시스턴트가 놓입니다. 어시스턴트는 모든 기기에서 이어지는 새 동기화 채팅이나, 이 기기에만 남는 새 로컬 채팅으로 시작할 수 있습니다.

공통 함수 formatPrice의 동작을 바꿔야 한다면, 함수를 우클릭하고 코드 그래프 표시(Show Code Graph)를 고릅니다. 호출자와 호출 대상이 목록으로 나옵니다. 채워진 점은 코드에서 직접 읽은 호출이고, 빈 점은 추론한 것이라 직접 확인해 보는 게 안전합니다. 변경 영향은 호출자의 호출자까지 따라가며, 이 예시에서는 "15 symbols · 14 files · 3 tests"로 나옵니다. 행을 클릭하면 해당 줄로 이동하고, 채팅으로 보내기를 누르면 그래프 전체를 어시스턴트에게 컨텍스트로 넘깁니다.

AI가 고친 파일을 확인하는 흐름도 있습니다. 소스 제어에서 수정된 파일을 열면, 마지막으로 AI가 작성한 파일에는 작은 로봇 표시가 붙고 아래 상태 줄에 모델 이름과 변경 이유가 나옵니다. 검토를 누르면 그 쓰기 직전에 저장된 사본과 나란히 비교한 diff가 열려서, 딱 그 변경만 볼 수 있습니다. 예시에서는 타임아웃이 30초에서 3초로 줄어 있었는데, 바로 위 주석에는 큰 사진 업로드는 20초 이상 걸린다고 적혀 있습니다. 커밋 전에 잡아내느냐에 따라 이후 수고가 크게 달라집니다.

내가 저장하지 않은 편집이 있는 파일에 에이전트가 쓴 경우에는, 어느 쪽을 몰래 고르지 않고 내 버전 유지와 디스크 버전 사용 중에서 선택하게 합니다.

다른 기능과의 연결

세 화면은 서로 오갈 수 있습니다. Wiki의 출처를 클릭하면 IDE의 해당 줄로, IDE의 이 폴더의 위키 버튼으로 다시 Wiki로 갑니다. IDE의 어시스턴트와 Wiki 페이지 옆 채팅은 Maestro를 기반으로 해서, 다른 Maestro 채팅과 같은 방식으로 질문하면 됩니다. 정확한 단어가 아니라 의미로 코드를 찾고 싶다면 인덱스 화면에서 로컬 검색 인덱스를 만들어 두면 Maestro가 그것을 활용합니다. Code의 실행을 팀에 공유할 준비가 되면 PR 열기로 그 브랜치의 PR을 엽니다.

각 화면은 제품 페이지의 데모에서 직접 눌러 볼 수 있습니다. Code와 IDE 페이지를 참고하세요.

자주 묻는 질문

데스크톱 앱이 꼭 필요한가요?
네. Code, IDE, Wiki는 로컬 폴더, Git worktree, 셸, 언어 서버를 사용하기 때문에 osFoundry 데스크톱 앱에서 동작합니다.

에이전트가 내 브랜치에 알아서 병합하기도 하나요?
아니요. 실행은 각자 전용 브랜치와 폴더에서 돌고, 내 브랜치는 병합 버튼을 눌렀을 때만 바뀝니다. 기본 설정에서는 테스트를 통과한 브랜치만 병합할 수 있습니다.

Wiki는 Notion 같은 팀 위키인가요?
아닙니다. 코드 저장소를 바탕으로 파일과 줄 번호 출처가 달린 문서를 쓰고, 코드가 바뀐 페이지에 표시를 붙이는 기능입니다. 아키텍처 개요나 온보딩 문서 같은 코드베이스 문서에 맞습니다.

충돌한 브랜치는 어떻게 되나요?
그대로 남습니다. 충돌 없는 브랜치만 먼저 병합하고, 충돌한 브랜치는 에이전트에게 그 위에서 다시 작업하게 하거나, 브랜치로 합치기에서 변경 블록을 골라 가져오면 됩니다.

데스크톱 앱은 osfoundry.io/ko/download에서 무료로 받을 수 있습니다.

title: Apa yang dilakukan Agent team di osFoundry, dan kapan satu agen sudah cukup
description:
Selasa pagi pukul 7:40, Priya punya pertanyaan yang harus dijawab sebelum makan siang karena direkturnya menunggu: apakah empat hari kerja seminggu benar-benar menjaga produktivitas? Dia bisa saja menempelkannya ke chatbot dan mendapat satu paragraf yang terdengar yakin. Tapi model yang mencari angkanya juga akan jadi model yang menilai apakah angka itu bisa dipercaya, dan model jarang membantah dirinya sendiri. Yang dia mau adalah satu orang mencari uji cobanya, orang lain menarik angkanya, dan orang ketiga mengembalikan apa pun yang tidak punya sumber.

Dua pintu masuk ke layar yang sama

osFoundry adalah aplikasi desktop untuk menjalankan pekerjaan AI di komputer kamu sendiri, dan ada dua cara yang mirip untuk menyerahkan pekerjaan ke agen. Agent (di sidebar tampil sebagai Single agent) adalah satu agen bernama dengan satu tujuan: kamu memberinya instruksi, ia mendapat ID sendiri seperti AG-0001L, dan setiap run yang dilakukannya tercatat sehingga bisa kamu telusuri nanti. Agent team menempatkan seorang leader di depan sekumpulan anggota spesialis. Leader merencanakan pekerjaan, memberikan tiap langkah ke satu anggota, lalu seorang reviewer memeriksa tiap langkah sebelum sampai ke kamu. Keduanya ada di sidebar di bawah Agents, bersebelahan, dan membuka layar yang sama. Bedanya hanya di jumlah anggota. Kalau kamu pernah ada di grup chat yang punya project manager, Agent team akan terasa familier. Bedanya, setiap pesan, serah terima, dan keputusan disimpan, dan kamu bisa scroll balik untuk melihatnya.

Melihat-lihat layar tim

Ini adalah sesi tim yang sudah selesai. Pertanyaan dan jawabannya adalah data contoh dari run demo.

  • Percakapan dengan leader (tengah). Header-nya bertuliskan "Leader · Orchestrate your team". Di sini kamu mengajukan pertanyaan sekali saja, dan di sini juga jawaban gabungannya muncul, dalam contoh ini berupa tabel dengan sumber di setiap baris, satu baris "Where sources disagree", dan satu baris "Not covered".
  • Tab sesi (bagian atas tengah). Chat, Team mail, Email, Handoffs, Sub-agents, Proposals, dan Files. Handoffs menunjukkan siapa menyerahkan pekerjaan ke siapa. Proposals berisi perubahan pada file atau pengaturan yang disarankan agen. Saran tidak diterapkan sampai disetujui.
  • Panel Agent session (kanan). Ada satu kartu per anggota, berisi apa yang diminta leader, tool yang dipanggil (web_fetch, web_search), dan hasilnya. Di bawah tiap hasil ada keputusan reviewer, misalnya "Approved". Di bagian atas ada pemilih run ("Run 1 · 07:40 AM") dan tombol Cards / Graph.
  • Tab Team roster. Ini daftar siapa saja yang boleh bertindak di sesi ini. Tim adalah daftar anggota, bukan workflow. Urutan kerjanya berasal dari rencana leader.
  • Rail sesi (kiri, disembunyikan di sini) dan inspector. Rail menampilkan semua sesi beserta ID-nya. Inspector punya tab Goal, Trigger, dan Hooks: untuk target akhir, apa yang memicu run, dan pengecekan di sekitar pekerjaan.

Tiga cara orang memakainya

Peneliti yang ingin setiap angka punya sumber

Priya membuka Agent team dan menekan New session. Di dialog New team session, dia membiarkan "Start from a team" terpilih dan memilih Deep Research Team dari daftar Team. Dialog memuat lima anggotanya (deep-research-agent, research-analyst, data-researcher, search-specialist, academic-researcher). Di bawah "Who leads" tampil Orchestrator, yang "plans the work up front, then delegates the steps to the agents below". Dia bisa menekan "make leader" di anggota mana pun untuk menjadikannya pemimpin.

Dia menekan Create, mengetik pertanyaannya di chat leader, lalu mengirimnya. Leader memecahnya jadi lima bagian: cari uji cobanya, studinya, angkanya, bukti yang berlawanan, lalu satu jawaban. Tiga anggota mulai bersamaan. Data Researcher menunggu daftar dari Search Specialist sebelum menarik angka. Saat Data Researcher melaporkan angka 40%, reviewer menandainya "Sent back" dengan alasan tidak ada sumber, tanggal, maupun ukurannya. Langkah itu dijalankan lagi, menemukan sumbernya, lalu disetujui.

Hasil akhirnya adalah satu jawaban di panel tengah, dan setiap angka di dalamnya sudah diperiksa oleh pihak lain selain agen yang menemukannya. Dia juga mendapat baris "Not covered" yang jujur, yang bisa langsung dia tempel ke catatan untuk direkturnya.

Developer solo yang terus menempelkan instruksi yang sama

Tom mengubah catatan rapat jadi daftar tugas beberapa kali seminggu, dan setiap kali dia harus menempelkan paragraf aturan yang sama ke chat lebih dulu. Pekerjaan ini tidak butuh tim. Yang dibutuhkan adalah satu agen yang ingat aturannya.

Dia membuka Single agent, menekan New session, dan tetap di tab Create in chat. Di kotak "New agent" dia menulis satu baris tentang apa yang dia butuhkan, lalu menekan Start. Chat yang terbuka adalah agen setup. Agen itu mengajukan beberapa pertanyaan, lalu mengusulkan nama, @handle, dan instruksi lengkap. Sebuah kartu muncul di atas kolom input berisi nama, handle, link Show instructions, dan tombol Create agent.

Dia membuka instruksinya dan memastikan aturan yang paling penting baginya ada di sana: jangan pernah menebak penanggung jawab atau tenggat. Lalu dia menekan Create agent. Chat yang sama sekarang menjadi agen itu. Saat dia menempelkan catatannya, penanggung jawab dan tanggal yang tidak ada ditandai sebagai kosong, tidak pernah ditebak. Sesi itu menyimpan Agent ID-nya di rail, dan lain kali dia cukup memilih agennya.

Release lead yang ingin tahu siapa mengerjakan apa

Dari mengurus rilis untuk tim produk kecil. Sesi timnya punya satu leader dan anggota bernama Release Drafter, Change Auditor, Docs Reviewer, QA Summarizer, dan Approval Prep. Masing-masing memegang satu bagian dari paket rilis.

Sebelum run, dia membuka tab Goal dan menekan Set a goal. Panel menjelaskan bahwa goal dipecah menjadi kriteria sukses yang awalnya gagal lalu berubah hijau saat agen memenuhinya. Sesi terus berjalan sampai semuanya lolos atau mencapai batas ronde. Dia menulis tiga kriteria, yang terakhir adalah paket persetujuan sudah lengkap. Selama anggota bekerja, dia mengecek Handoffs untuk mengikuti rantai dari leader ke tiap anggota dan kembali. Dia juga mengecek Proposals untuk perubahan konfigurasi yang disarankan anggota, dan tidak ada yang diterapkan tanpa dia. Dia bisa mengarahkan leader kapan saja dengan membalas di chat-nya, dan Pause di header panel menahan run selama dia meninjau.

Di akhir, dia punya paket rilis plus catatan siapa yang menyusun, mengaudit, dan menyetujui tiap bagian. Catatan itu bisa dia tunjukkan ke siapa pun yang bertanya bagaimana satu baris bisa masuk ke release notes.

Ke mana arahnya di bagian lain aplikasi

Agent dan Agent team adalah tempat pekerjaan dimulai. Sessions adalah tempat kamu memantaunya. Board itu menampilkan setiap sesi chat, agen, tim, dan terminal sebagai satu kartu, dikelompokkan ke Running, Needs you, Paused, Idle, Done, dan Failed sesuai apa yang benar-benar sedang dilakukan sesi itu.

Kalau pekerjaan tim yang sama harus dijalankan berulang kali, Loop membungkus sebuah tim dengan trigger, batasan, dan catatan per ronde tentang kriteria mana yang lolos. Graphs dipakai untuk pekerjaan yang jalurnya bergantung pada apa yang terjadi di tengah jalan. Percakapan dengan leader adalah chat Maestro, jadi jawaban tim bisa berlanjut ke pekerjaan Maestro kamu yang lain. Link Enable sync di sesi menghubungkannya ke channel pesan proyek, tempat orang dan agen bisa berbicara di satu tempat. Baca lebih lanjut di halaman fitur Agents dan ringkasan sesi agen.

Pertanyaan yang sering diajukan pengguna baru

Kapan sebaiknya pakai satu agen daripada tim?
Pakai satu agen kalau pekerjaannya satu tugas jelas dengan aturan tetap, seperti merapikan format catatan atau menulis balasan dengan satu gaya. Pakai tim kalau pekerjaannya punya bagian-bagian yang butuh tool berbeda, atau kalau kamu ingin ada reviewer terpisah yang memeriksa hasilnya sebelum kamu melihatnya.

Bisakah saya mengubah tim setelah sesi dimulai?
Tidak. Dialog New team session menyebutkan bahwa tim "is fixed for this session's life". Di dalam dialog kamu masih bisa menambah atau menghapus agen dan memilih siapa yang memimpin sebelum menekan Create. Untuk memakai susunan anggota lain, mulai sesi baru.

Apakah ada yang berjalan di cloud?
Form New session menawarkan run Local dan Isolated. Di sana disebutkan bahwa keduanya berjalan di komputer kamu dengan key milik kamu sendiri dan tidak ada yang dikirim ke cloud. Riwayat chat bersifat lokal secara default.

Bisakah agen menulis ulang instruksinya sendiri?
Mereka bisa menyarankan perubahan, yang muncul di Proposals. Proposal bukan konfigurasi yang sudah diterima. Apakah agen boleh mengubah prompt-nya sendiri adalah pengaturan terpisah.

Aplikasi desktopnya bisa kamu unduh di osfoundry.io/id/download.

title: When Your AI Agent Starts Shopping: Designing the Invisible Marketplace.
description:
When Your AI Agent Starts Shopping: Designing the Invisible Marketplace

The next shift in commerce will not be “more ads in chat.” It will be agents negotiating with agents.

Instead of clicking through search results, comparing tabs, and checking out manually, users will increasingly delegate bounded commercial missions to personal AI agents: “Find a durable laptop under €1,500,” “renew my insurance before the storm,” or “keep my monthly household spending under €100.” Brands will still compete for attention—but the decisive audience will increasingly be the user’s agent.

This is not just a UX change. It is an architectural shift from human-facing interfaces to agent-readable commerce.

From Ads to Agent-Readable Commerce

Traditional digital marketing interrupts humans: banners, pop-ups, retargeting, email blasts. Agentic commerce changes the unit of competition.

A brand no longer wins only because its landing page looks persuasive. It wins because its product data, availability, delivery terms, return policy, warranty, and checkout flow can be interpreted reliably by an agent.

The Universal Commerce Protocol (UCP) is designed around this idea. It provides a shared language for agents, merchants, and payment providers across discovery, cart, checkout, orders, and post-purchase support.[1][2]

In practical terms, “marketing” becomes a data and trust problem:

Traditional commerce Agentic commerce
Persuasive landing page Structured, verifiable product data
Banner or retargeting ad Relevant offer surfaced through an agent
Human compares tabs Agent compares options against user policy
Checkout form Delegated, scoped checkout
Support ticket Agent-readable order, refund, and dispute state
Brand trust Machine-verifiable trust signals

The important distinction is that agents do not eliminate brands. They change what brands must expose: not just a beautiful storefront, but a trustworthy commercial API.

The Invisible Marketplace

Think of the emerging stack as an invisible marketplace with three distinct actors:

User
  │
  ├─ Personal Agent
  │    • Interprets intent
  │    • Holds preferences and constraints
  │    • Evaluates offers
  │    • Requests approval when needed
  │
  ├─ Merchant / Brand Agent
  │    • Publishes catalog and policies
  │    • Presents offers
  │    • Handles fulfillment and support
  │
  └─ Commerce / Payment Layer
       • Cart, checkout, identity, payment authorization
       • Auditability and dispute resolution

The personal agent represents the user. The merchant agent represents the seller. They must not be conflated.

If the user’s agent receives incentives directly from brands, it stops being a user representative and becomes a hidden sales channel. The design challenge is not “make AI sell better.” It is: how do we let agents transact without turning the user’s advocate into an advertiser?

Ambient Intelligence Meets Commerce

Ambient intelligence gives agents context beyond a chat prompt: location, time, weather, traffic, local movement, device state, and historical preferences.

This can make commerce genuinely useful. For example, an insurer could detect elevated storm risk in a user’s area and propose a temporary upgrade to home-content coverage before damage occurs. That is proactive service—not interruption.

WPP’s integration of Google Earth AI illustrates the direction: geospatial signals such as weather, traffic, places, and local movement patterns can be combined with first-party data to estimate local demand and tailor marketing and operations.[3][4]

But ambient context is also a manipulation surface. An agent that knows you are tired, financially stressed, near a store, or recently researching a product can make an offer feel urgent and personal. The ethical line is clear:

Ambient signals should improve the user’s decision, not exploit the user’s vulnerability.

The Core Primitive: Purchase Mandates

Do not give an agent a vague instruction like “buy me a laptop.”

Give it a purchase mandate: a machine-readable contract that defines the goal, constraints, budget, authority, and audit requirements.

{
  "goal": "Buy a developer laptop",
  "budget": {
    "currency": "EUR",
    "max_total": 1500,
    "max_single_transaction": 1500
  },
  "constraints": {
    "allowed_merchant_tiers": ["trusted"],
    "min_warranty_months": 24,
    "max_delivery_days": 5,
    "return_policy_days": 30
  },
  "authority": {
    "auto_purchase": false,
    "user_approval_required_above_eur": 500,
    "payment_credential": "single_use_scoped_token"
  },
  "audit": {
    "record_decision_reason": true,
    "record_rejected_alternatives": true,
    "retain_receipts": true
  }
}

This structure turns “AI autonomy” into something governable.

A purchase mandate should answer four questions:

  • What is the user trying to achieve?
  • What constraints apply?
  • What can the agent do without asking?
  • What evidence must be retained?

Without these boundaries, “agent commerce” becomes autonomous spending with better branding.

Protocol Layers: MCP, UCP, and ACP

A common mistake is treating MCP, UCP, and ACP as competing standards. They solve different layers of the problem.

Layer Protocol Primary role
Tool and data access MCP Connect agents to tools, APIs, and context
Agent-to-agent coordination A2A Delegate tasks across specialized agents
Commerce workflow UCP Catalog, cart, checkout, orders, support
Checkout and payment relay ACP Agent-mediated purchase and credential handling

UCP uses a layered model: services organize domains, capabilities define actions such as checkout and cart, and extensions make features such as fulfillment reusable. It is transport-agnostic and supports bindings including REST, MCP, and Agent2Agent.[1]

ACP, meanwhile, focuses on programmatic exchange between buyers, their agents, and sellers to complete purchases. It defines interfaces for checkout and secure credential relay, while merchants retain their existing backend and payment-processing models.[5]

A useful mental model is:

MCP: “Connect me to tools and data.”
A2A: “Let agents collaborate.”
UCP: “Let us run a commerce transaction.”
ACP: “Let us complete a checkout securely.”

A Practical Reference Architecture

Here is a pragmatic architecture for an agent-ready commerce product:

┌───────────────────────────────┐
│ User Interface / Voice / Chat │
└──────────────┬────────────────┘
               │
┌──────────────▼────────────────┐
│ Personal Agent Runtime        │
│ - Intent parsing              │
│ - Policy engine               │
│ - Memory and preferences      │
│ - Approval workflow           │
└──────────────┬────────────────┘
               │
┌──────────────▼────────────────┐
│ Commerce Orchestration Layer  │
│ - UCP / ACP adapters          │
│ - Merchant discovery          │
│ - Offer comparison            │
│ - Order state machine         │
└──────────────┬────────────────┘
               │
┌──────────────▼────────────────┐
│ Merchant / Brand Agent APIs   │
│ - Catalog                     │
│ - Inventory                   │
│ - Pricing                     │
│ - Fulfillment                 │
│ - Returns and support         │
└──────────────┬────────────────┘
               │
┌──────────────▼────────────────┐
│ Payments and Audit Layer      │
│ - Scoped payment credentials  │
│ - Risk controls               │
│ - Receipts                    │
│ - Decision logs               │
└───────────────────────────────┘

The most important architectural rule is separation:

Decisioning, authorization, and execution must be separable.

An agent may recommend a product. It may prepare a cart. But payment execution should require an explicit, scoped authorization—especially above a threshold.

OpenAI’s delegated payment model, for example, uses a single-use delegated payment payload with allowances; a payment service provider or vault returns a token scoped to that delegated payment, which is then used to complete the transaction.[6]

Agent-Ready Product Data

If you build an e-commerce platform, start treating your catalog as an agent-facing product surface.

At minimum, expose:

  • Canonical product ID and variant ID
  • Real-time price, currency, taxes, and fees
  • Stock status and fulfillment estimates
  • Shipping cost and delivery window
  • Return window and conditions
  • Warranty and certification data
  • Seller identity and reputation signals
  • Machine-readable policies
  • Idempotency keys for cart and order operations

A shopping agent needs to answer questions such as:

  • Is this the same product as the one the user saw earlier?
  • Is the final price actually €899, or €899 plus shipping and tax?
  • Can it arrive before Friday?
  • Can the user return it after opening it?
  • Is this seller authorized to sell the product?
  • What happens if the item is damaged?

If those answers live in marketing copy, PDFs, or inconsistent product pages, the agent will guess. Guessing is how bad purchases happen.

State Machines Beat “Smart” Prompts

LLMs are good at interpretation, but unreliable as the sole source of transactional truth.

Do not let a model decide whether an order was placed. Model commerce as an explicit state machine:

draft
  → awaiting_user_approval
  → authorized
  → payment_pending
  → ordered
  → fulfilled
  → delivered
  → return_requested
  → refunded
  → failed

Each transition should be validated by deterministic business logic—not by a prompt.

For example:

IF state == "awaiting_user_approval"
AND amount > user_approval_threshold
THEN require explicit user approval

IF state == "authorized"
AND payment_token.is_expired
THEN reject checkout

IF checkout_request.retried
THEN use idempotency_key

The model can help draft the intent, explain options, or summarize an order. The transactional system must enforce the rules.

Trust Is a Product Feature

“Trust” is often treated as a compliance afterthought. In agentic commerce, it is the product.

A credible agent-commerce system needs:

  • Provenance: Where did each product claim come from?
  • Disclosure: Is the recommendation sponsored, commissioned, or ranked for commercial reasons?
  • Authority: What exactly is the agent allowed to do?
  • Scope: Which merchant, amount, and time window does a payment credential cover?
  • Reversibility: Can the user cancel, dispute, or return the outcome?
  • Auditability: Can the user see why an option was selected and which alternatives were rejected?

This matters because visibility rules inside AI-generated answers can create competition and consumer-protection concerns. Regulators have specifically flagged the need for clear, objective, and non-discriminatory conditions governing content visibility in AI agent responses.

A simple UI pattern:

Recommended: Laptop A
Why: Best balance of price, delivery time, warranty, and return policy.
Alternatives considered: Laptop B, Laptop C
Commercial relationship: None / Affiliate commission disclosed
User approval required: Yes, because total exceeds €500

That is more trustworthy than a polished “Buy now” button.

Anti-Patterns to Avoid

1. The omni-agent

Do not build one agent that discovers, decides, pays, fulfills, supports, and resolves disputes. Separate high-risk capabilities.

2. Commission-optimized recommendations

If the ranking objective is “highest affiliate payout,” the agent is not optimizing for the user. Make the commercial objective explicit and auditable.

3. Persistent payment access

Never give an agent standing access to a card, bank account, or wallet. Use scoped, expiring, single-use credentials with hard limits.

4. Black-box personalization

“Because you might like it” is not sufficient. Users should be able to inspect the inputs and rules behind consequential recommendations.

5. Ambient coercion

Countdown timers, artificial scarcity, and fear-based urgency become worse when an agent can act instantly. Ambient marketing must not become ambient pressure.

A Practical Build Checklist

If you are building toward agent-ready commerce, prioritize these capabilities:

  • Publish structured product, inventory, pricing, and fulfillment data.
  • Support stable IDs and versioned APIs.
  • Expose return, warranty, and dispute policies as data, not PDFs.
  • Implement idempotency for cart, checkout, and order operations.
  • Separate recommendation, approval, and payment execution.
  • Use scoped payment credentials with explicit limits.
  • Log the decision reason, considered alternatives, and policy version.
  • Build user-facing controls for memory, permissions, budgets, and revocation.
  • Design for human override at every consequential step.
  • Make disclosures visible in the same surface where the recommendation appears.

UCP is explicitly intended to reduce bespoke integrations across consumer surfaces, businesses, and payment providers, while ACP enables agents to conduct checkout and securely relay credentials.[1][5]

Example: The Pre-Storm Insurance Offer

Imagine a user living in a flood-prone area. Their agent receives a weather-risk signal.

A responsible flow looks like this:

1. Ambient signal: elevated storm risk in the user’s area
2. Personal agent checks policy and coverage
3. Agent identifies a relevant coverage gap
4. Merchant agent provides upgrade options
5. Personal agent compares cost, coverage, and exclusions
6. Agent presents a recommendation and reason
7. User approves or rejects the purchase
8. System records the decision trail

The agent does not say:

“Buy now—storm is coming!”

It says:

“Your current policy excludes water damage to stored belongings. A temporary upgrade costs €18 and covers up to €2,000. I recommend reviewing it before Friday. Approval required.”

That is the difference between ambient intelligence and ambient manipulation.

The Real Competitive Advantage

The next generation of commerce will not be won by whoever shows the most persuasive ad.

It will be won by whoever builds the most trustworthy interface between human intent and commercial execution.

For developers, that means designing systems where an agent can answer:

  • Whose interests does this agent serve?
  • What authority does it have?
  • What data influenced this recommendation?
  • Why was this option selected?
  • Can the user reverse or audit the outcome?

If you can answer those questions clearly, you are not merely building an AI shopping assistant.

You are building the trust layer for the invisible marketplace.

Citations:
[1] Open rails for agentic commerce at Open Source Summit ... https://opensource.googleblog.com/2026/06/open-rails-for-agentic-commerce-at-open-source-summit-north-america-2026.html
[2] A new way to shop: Introducing a more intuitive, agentic ... https://blog.google/intl/en-ca/products/explore-get-answers/a-new-way-to-shop-introducing-a-more-intuitive-agentic-shopping-experience-for-consumers-and-retailers-in-canada/
[3] WPP and Google Enhance Consumer Insights with Google Earth AI https://www.wppmedia.com/hr/news/WPP-tager-et-nyt-skridt-i-kampen-om-forbrugerforst%C3%A5elsen
[4] News | WPP https://www.wpp.com/en/news??loaded=330
[5] Documentation https://www.agenticcommerce.dev/docs
[6] Delegated Payment Spec – Agentic Commerce https://developers.openai.com/commerce/specs/payment
[7] Google Universal Commerce Protocol (UCP) for Lodging https://developers.google.com/hotels/ucp
